chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The one looking after the sacrificial animal of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was Najiya ibn Jundab al-Khuzai al-Aslami. And the one who shaved the head of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) during his Hajj was Ma'mar ibn Abdullah ibn Haratha ibn Nasr ibn Awf ibn Uwayj ibn Adi ibn Ka'b. He said: And when he was shaving the hair of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) during the Hajj, the Quraysh said: O Ma'mar! The ears [head] of the Messenger of Allah are in your hand, and the blade is in your hand. Ma'mar said: By Allah, I consider it a great favor from Allah upon me. He said: And Ma'mar was the one who used to saddle the camel for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So the Messenger of Allah said to him: O Ma'mar, the saddle is slack this night. Ma'mar said: May my father and mother be ransomed for you, I tightened it as I always do, but one of those who is jealous of my position with you, O Messenger of Allah, wished that you replace me [with someone else]. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: I would never do that.

key_terms.معمر بن عبدالله: Ma'mar ibn Abdullah, the shaver of the Prophet's head
key_terms.ناجية بن جندب: Najiya ibn Jundab, keeper of the sacrificial animal

ai.seo_question: Who shaved the Prophet's head during the Farewell Hajj and what does the story of the loose saddle reveal about Ma'mar's status?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Ibn Abi Umair, provides specific biographical details regarding the Farewell Hajj, identifying Najiya ibn Jundab and Ma'mar ibn Abdullah as key attendants of the Prophet. It underscores Ma'mar's high status and the Prophet's personal assurance against replacement, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the loyalty of close companions (Sahaba) and the Prophet's awareness of subtle social dynamics like jealousy among his circle. The incident illustrates the concept of *tawassul* through trusted servants and the Prophet's intimate knowledge of his household's affairs.
